bug_semantics: indiserver accepts unauthenticated TCP on port 7624 and feeds every received byte into lilxml. In oneXMLchar() INCLOSETAG, mismatched closing-tag names that growString() accumulated without a cap are interpolated with unbounded sprintf() into the caller's fixed 1024-byte stack errmsg/ynot buffer (char err[1024] at MsgQueue::readFromFd / historically indiserver readFromClient). A single malformed packet such as <AAA...600>x</BBB...600> writes past the 1024-byte slot and terminates the daemon (CWE-121, availability-only as disclosed).
flaw_origin: The overflow write is the 2008 first import of liblilxml: indi/libs/lilxml.c oneXMLchar() already did sprintf(errmsg, "Line %d: closing tag %s does not match %s", ln, endtag.s, tag.s) over unbounded growString() tokens, and lilxml.h already showed callers allocating char errmsg[1024]. Later commits only renamed errmsg->ynot, moved/reindented the file, and split the 1024-byte TCP caller into MsgQueue.cpp; they did not first write the mechanism.
